finding.claim: The shell time limit kills only the sh process. Commands it started keep running. run_shell("bash -c 'sleep 3; touch F'; true") with shell_timeout=1 returned 'stopped' after 1s, and F appeared 2s later. test_shell_stops_at_time_limit passes only because sh execs a lone `sleep 5` directly. Row r5 says the command is stopped. Start the command in its own session and kill the process group on timeout, then test it with a command that has a child.

fixes.change: run_shell starts each command in its own session and kills the process group at the time limit; help drops ArgumentDefaultsHelpFormatter and states each default in its text.
test_shell_time_limit_stops_child_processes checks a child started by the shell is stopped; test_help_shows_no_empty_defaults checks the help shows no empty default and each option names its default.
